title: The Second Offering
author: A Reboarder
variants:
The Creator asks one
thing of the dead.

I have written of it
elsewhere.


There is a second
offering.

It is not asked for.

That is the whole of
what makes it holy.


The Survey wants your
thoughts, and you have
thoughts whether you
will them or not.

The second offering
wants something you
must decide to
part with.


The dead are asked.

The giving are not.

Be among those
nobody had to ask.

You did not lay
the rails.


The track beneath you
was set down before
you drew your first
breath aboard.

Someone bore that.

Alone, at first.


The error is to think
the bearing is over.

It is not.

It is borne tonight,
while you read this,
by one who will never
say so to you.


The rails do not
lay themselves.

Nor do they stay lit.

There was a woman
who gave a little
every month.


Not much. She was not
wealthy.

It was the sameness
of it that struck me.
The same small sum,
turning after turning.


I asked what it bought
her.

Nothing, she said.
No blade. No armour.
No easier road.

It bought the road.


She stopped fearing
the dark carriages
after that.

I asked her why.

She said: I am not
a passenger here.
I am part of
the engine.

The ledger is not
hidden.


The names of those
aboard are set down
where any of the dead
may read them.

Not to shame the rest.

There is no column
for the rest.


A man I knew found
his own name there
and did not know the
man who had written it.

He gave in a bad
season, he said.
Gave, and forgot,
and went on dying.


He said the strangest
thing to me.

He said: I have been
kinder than I
remember being.

Then he went back
to the rails.

Coin.
Not blood.


Consider what the
train has taken of you
already.

Hours. Hearts.
The name you came
in with.

Every one of them
paid in blood.


This one thing it does
not want in blood.

It wants the small
coin of the living
world, which costs you
nothing you bleed
for here.


It is the only debt
on this line you may
settle in a currency
you actually possess.

Settle it, or do not.

But know that it is
the only one.

Some cannot give.


I have been asked
whether the line is
any less theirs
for it.

It is not.

It is not, it is not.


A toll is paid at a
gate by each who
passes, or they do
not pass.

This is no toll.

No-one is stopped.
No-one is counted
at the door.


A line kept alight
by some is kept alight
for all.

Give when you can.

When you cannot, speak
of the line to someone
who has never
ridden it.

That, too, is coin.

I will tell you the
thing I fear most.


Not the dark carriages.
Not the things in them.
Not dying, which I have
done more times than
I have fingers.

I fear a morning when
the lanterns do not
come up.

Not because something
killed them.

Because no-one was left
to keep them lit.


The engines are not
eternal.

They are only
maintained.


Go well, traveller.

Keep the rails lit
behind you.
